items.summary: For 2026, the standard deduction is $16,100 for single and married filing separately, $32,200 for married filing jointly and qualifying surviving spouse, and $24,150 for head of household.
For 2026 single filers, ordinary income brackets run from 10% through 37%; the top 37% bracket begins above $640,600 of taxable income.
For 2026 married filing jointly, ordinary income brackets run from 10% through 37%; the top 37% bracket begins above $768,700 of taxable income.
The federal itemized deduction for state and local taxes is limited by a statutory SALT cap; taxpayers should verify the applicable cap and filing-status rules for the return year.
Cash charitable contributions to qualifying public charities may be limited by AGI percentage rules; excess contributions may require carryforward treatment.
The student loan interest deduction can reduce income by up to $2,500 when statutory income and loan-use requirements are met.
Traditional IRA contribution deductibility depends on compensation, filing status, workplace retirement plan coverage, and modified AGI phaseouts.
A Roth conversion generally includes taxable pre-tax retirement amounts in income in the year converted; it is not subject to the annual Roth contribution limit.
Section 199A may allow up to a 20% qualified business income deduction, subject to taxable-income thresholds, business type, wage, and property limitations.
For 2026, the QBI threshold amount for single filers is $276,750 before phase-in limits apply.
For 2026, the QBI threshold amount for married filing jointly is $553,500 before phase-in limits apply.
Alternative Minimum Tax is a parallel federal tax calculation using AMT income, AMT exemptions, and exemption phaseouts; higher-income taxpayers may need a separate AMT check.
Earned Income Tax Credit eligibility depends on earned income, investment income, filing status, valid SSNs, and qualifying-child rules.
The Child Tax Credit can be up to $2,000 per qualifying child, with refundability and phaseout rules depending on income and eligibility.
The child and dependent care credit may apply to qualifying care expenses paid so the taxpayer and spouse, if any, can work or look for work.
The American Opportunity Tax Credit may apply to qualified education expenses for an eligible student in the first four years of postsecondary education, subject to income limits.
The Lifetime Learning Credit may apply to qualified tuition and related expenses for eligible students, subject to income limitations and coordination rules.
Net Investment Income Tax is 3.8% on the lesser of net investment income or modified AGI above the statutory threshold for the filing status.
Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends may be taxed at preferential 0%, 15%, or 20% federal rates, depending on taxable income and filing status.
Certain collectibles gains may be taxed at a maximum federal rate of 28%, rather than the regular long-term capital gains rate schedule.
Kiddie tax rules can tax a child's unearned income using parent-linked computations when age, support, student, and income tests are met.
Additional Medicare Tax applies at 0.9% above statutory wages, compensation, and self-employment income thresholds; employers withhold it on wages over $200,000.
For 2026, Social Security tax applies to covered wages up to the contribution and benefit base of $184,500.
Employee FICA generally includes 6.2% Social Security tax up to the wage base and 1.45% Medicare tax on covered wages, before any Additional Medicare Tax.
Estimated tax safe harbor rules can reduce underpayment penalties when withholding and estimated payments meet prior-year or current-year tax thresholds.
Individual federal income tax returns are generally due April 15 unless the date is moved by a weekend, legal holiday, disaster relief, or special rule.
A valid automatic extension generally extends the time to file an individual federal return to October 15, but it does not extend the time to pay tax.
The first federal estimated tax installment for a calendar-year individual is generally due April 15.
The second federal estimated tax installment for a calendar-year individual is generally due June 15.
The third federal estimated tax installment for a calendar-year individual is generally due September 15.
The fourth federal estimated tax installment for a calendar-year individual is generally due January 15 of the following year.
Employers generally must furnish Forms W-2 to employees by January 31 after the calendar year and file required copies with the Social Security Administration.
Many Forms 1099 have January 31 recipient deadlines, but exact filing deadlines depend on the form type and filing method.
U.S. citizens and resident aliens abroad may qualify for an automatic two-month filing extension, but interest can still accrue on unpaid tax from the original due date.
For 2026, the maximum foreign earned income exclusion is $132,900 per qualifying person.
The physical presence test generally requires 330 full days in foreign countries during a 12-month period, along with a tax home in a foreign country.
The bona fide residence test generally requires bona fide residence in a foreign country for an uninterrupted period that includes an entire tax year.
The foreign housing exclusion or deduction may apply to qualified foreign housing expenses above a base amount, subject to location-based and statutory limits.
The foreign tax credit can reduce U.S. tax for qualifying foreign income taxes, but separate limitation categories and Form 1116 rules may apply.
California uses progressive personal income tax rate schedules and generally starts from federal AGI with California-specific adjustments and deductions.
California's modeled 2025 base rate schedule reaches 12.3%; the separate 1% mental health services tax over $1,000,000 is not modeled in the MVP engine.
New York taxes resident income using progressive state brackets; local New York City or Yonkers taxes are separate from the MVP state calculation.
New York City resident income tax can apply in addition to New York State tax and is not part of the current MVP state-income-tax engine.
Massachusetts imposes a 4% surtax on taxable income over $1,000,000 in addition to its regular personal income tax rules.
New Jersey's gross income tax uses a state gross-income base rather than simply federal AGI, and the MVP engine models a simplified gross-income start point.
Washington has no broad personal income tax, but it imposes a capital gains excise tax on certain long-term capital gains above the annual standard deduction.
Oregon's modeled income tax base subtracts Oregon standard deduction and a data-driven federal income tax subtraction that phases out by AGI.
Oregon is generally known for not having a statewide general sales tax, but it does impose a progressive personal income tax.
Illinois uses a flat individual income tax rate; the MVP rule data uses a 4.95% flat state income tax rate.
Pennsylvania personal income tax is modeled as a flat 3.07% tax on gross-income-style taxable income.
Connecticut generally taxes capital gains as part of state income rather than applying a separate preferential capital-gains rate in the MVP model.
Hawaii has progressive personal income tax brackets and a high top marginal rate compared with many states.
Texas does not impose a broad personal income tax, so the MVP state income tax calculation returns no state income tax for Texas residents.
Florida does not impose a broad personal income tax, so the MVP state income tax calculation returns no state income tax for Florida residents.
Nevada does not impose a broad personal income tax, so the MVP state income tax calculation returns no state income tax for Nevada residents.
Wyoming does not impose a broad personal income tax, so the MVP state income tax calculation returns no state income tax for Wyoming residents.
State residency can depend on domicile, statutory-resident day counts, permanent place of abode, and state-specific facts; it is separate from federal tax residency.
Domicile generally asks where a taxpayer's permanent home is, while statutory residency can apply based on days and abode even without domicile.
Economic nexus can be triggered by state-specific sales dollars, transaction counts, marketplace rules, or physical presence, and thresholds vary by state.
Convenience-of-the-employer rules can source remote workdays to the employer state in some jurisdictions; this requires state-specific analysis beyond federal AGI.
Some states use day-count thresholds or safe harbors for residency or sourcing, but the thresholds and evidence requirements vary by state.
Digital asset gain or loss depends on proceeds, cost basis, fees, and holding period; taxpayers need records that identify units disposed of.
A digital asset held more than one year before sale or exchange generally produces long-term capital gain or loss; one year or less is short-term.
Form 1099-DA is intended for broker reporting of digital asset proceeds; taxpayers still need their own basis and transaction records.
Staking, mining, or similar digital asset rewards may create ordinary income when received, with later gain or loss measured from the income-included basis.
Some NFT transactions may involve collectible property, which can require separate federal capital-gain rate analysis and is not automatically the regular crypto path.
Self-employment tax generally combines Social Security and Medicare tax on net earnings from self-employment, subject to wage-base and Additional Medicare Tax rules.
A taxpayer generally must file Schedule SE when net earnings from self-employment are $400 or more, subject to special exceptions.
RSUs generally create ordinary wage income when shares vest and are delivered, and later sale creates capital gain or loss from the post-vest basis.
RSU double-tax risk often comes from reporting vest income on Form W-2 while also using an unadjusted broker basis on sale; basis reconciliation is important.
Incentive stock option exercise can create AMT adjustment exposure even when regular tax income is deferred until a qualifying or disqualifying disposition.
Nonqualified stock option exercise generally creates ordinary compensation income equal to spread at exercise, with later sale producing capital gain or loss.
A Section 83(b) election can accelerate income inclusion for restricted property and generally must be filed within 30 days of transfer.
